it-a700.comment: Clean five-finger positions (D3 and C3) with the shift at the bar line; the leaps E4-D3 and G2-C2 come from the music and are taken with the natural fingers.

objections.problem: Fingers 3 and 2 cannot span the major sixth C3-A3; the same chord is taken 5+1 just before and after.
Finger 3 is assigned to both A2 and E3 of one chord; the thumb should keep E3 from the octave before.

it-6efc.comment: Two impossible chords: the repeated C3+A3 must stay 5+1 throughout, and the closing A2+E3 wants 3+1 with the thumb holding its place on E3.

objections.problem: Thumb and 2 cross back and forth on D5-C#5-D5 at ornament speed, then 3 crosses again; 4-3-4-3 keeps the turn in place.

it-c75c.comment: Sound apart from the opening ornament; fingered 4-3-4-3, the descent continues naturally with 2 and 1 to A4.

objections.problem: Finger 5 hops from G5 to C6 at sixteenth speed, breaking the legato at the top of the rising broken chord.

it-fc5d.comment: The thumb-under start in bar 5 neatly fits that arpeggio into one octave; bar 6 only needs the hop removed. The 4-5 trill in bar 7 is weak but tolerable for so short an ornament.

objections.problem: Thumb on Eb5 between two E5s, then 5 lands a semitone above it at sixteenth speed: cramped, and thumb on a black key.
Rising C#5-Eb5-E5 fingered 5-4-3: 5 takes C#5 while still holding E5, then 4 and 3 land above the held 5.

it-47bb.comment: Holding the upper voice with 5 while the lower voice moves is well planned, but bar 7 beat 4 cannot be played as written; reuse the 4-5 from R10-R11 for the Eb5-E5 figure.

objections.problem: Thumb passes under 3 onto black F#5 inside a 32nd-note turn, then 3 crosses back; R2-R4 already shows the in-place 4-3-4.
C5-B4-C5 fingered 3-5-4: 5 must pass under 3 and 4 back over 5 at 32nd-note speed.

it-fcb3.comment: Both ornaments should be fingered in one position; as written the second turn is clumsy and the mordent in bar 6 cannot be played.

objections.problem: Rising G4-G#4-Bb4 fingered 5-4-3 against the held thumb reverses finger order; the sequence in bar 13 uses 2-3-4.
Thumb holds Bb4 while 2 plays G4 below it, then the thumb must take Eb4 before Bb4 ends.
Thumb assigned to both notes of the octave G3+G4.

it-366b.comment: Bar 13 is a sequence of bar 12 a tone higher and should share its fingering (3 2 1 2 3 4 2 1); the final octave needs 1+5.

objections.problem: With F5 held by 5, taking C#5 with 4 forces a major-third 4-5 spread twice; 3 sits there naturally.

it-75dd.comment: The melody fingering (4-5 for Eb5-F5) is well chosen; the G#4+Bb5 ninth is a stretch imposed by the music, not by the fingering.

objections.problem: Finger 4 is given to both Eb3 and G#3 in the same chord; one finger cannot cover a fourth.
Finger 3 plays G#5 then Eb5 in consecutive eighths, a hop of a fourth; finger 2 on Eb5 keeps the line connected.
Same chord on beats 2 and 3 fingered 4-3-2 then 4-2-1; 4-3-2 stretches 3-2 across a fourth. Use 4-2-1 both times.

it-ff11.comment: The waltz layout and the 3-2-1 repeated-note fingering on Eb5 are good, but the bar 25 beat 3 chord is impossible and the two bar 24 chords should match.

objections.problem: G4 is held as a dotted half on finger 3 while the same finger must play F4 in the turn below it.
A4 is still held by finger 4 when Bb4, a semitone higher, is taken by finger 3: a long finger crossing a long finger.

it-f0a3.comment: Bars 5-7 are clean. Bars 8 and 9 overlook the sustained G4 and A4: the fingers holding them cannot be reused for the moving notes.

objections.problem: Root-position triad G#4-C5-Eb5 on 1-3-4; standard 1-3-5 also lets the top line move Eb5-C#5 legato with 5-4.

it-c031.comment: Sound chordal fingering: the thumb anchors each sonority, 2 on G#4 gives a legato lower line where it matters, and the octaves are uniformly 1-2-5 around the repeated Bb4.

it-5d7f.comment: Both hands stay in natural five-finger positions, shifting only at the octave leaps, the rest and the held notes; usable as is.

objections.problem: The third falling third switches from 2-1 to 3-2; keeping 2-1 puts the thumb on G4, ready for the bar 30 position.

it-9bba.comment: Sound and idiomatic; the 3-over-thumb crossing onto F4 in bar 30 is well placed.

it-1269.comment: Standard first-inversion arpeggio and triad shapes in both hands; the jump down to E4-G4 at bar 18 beat 3.5 is unavoidable and sensibly placed.

objections.problem: E5-Eb5 on 3-2 then E5 on 5 forces a jump of the hand within three sixteenths; 5-4-5 stays put and matches later Eb5-E5.
Finger 4 holds D5 and C#5 a minor seventh above the thumb on E4 and Eb4; finger the bar-8 sighs 4-5 as in bar 7.

it-4654.comment: Thoughtful two-voice fingering overall, and thumb slides in the lower voice are acceptable here, but the opening shift and the bar 8 stretches should be fixed.

objections.problem: Finger 2 holds G#3 for the whole bar yet must also play A3 on beat 2; bar 23 correctly uses 3 on G#3.

it-0df4.comment: Bar 23 shows the right solution and bar 21 should match it; otherwise the positions are economical.

it-e31b.comment: Sound and economical: each bar sits in one hand frame and the repeated bars match. Using 5+3 in bar 24 sensibly keeps the thumb off C#4.

it-a4b6.comment: Practical throughout: the unavoidable shift to the descending arpeggio falls on the leap, and the E3-G#3-B3 frame on 5-3-1 under the thirds is standard. The 5-to-5 bass leap into bar 9 is normal at this tempo.

objections.problem: 3-2-1 on G#3-C#4-F4 puts a perfect fourth between fingers 3 and 2; 4-2-1, as in bar 26, is comfortable.

it-f224.comment: Good waltz-bass fingering overall, with the 5 kept for the bass and the chords placed without hops. Only the bar-28 chord needs the easier 4-2-1 shape.

objections.problem: Finger 4 plays F5 then E5 in consecutive sixteenths; the descending run F5-C5 is simply 4-3-2-1.
Finger 3 cannot play G#4 and B4 at once; 2+4 crosses over the thumb from C5 and leaves the thumb free for E4.

it-0c9e.comment: The G#4+B4 dyad on one finger is impossible and the 4-4 on F5-E5 is a slip. The thirds in bar 15 follow the standard 2/4, 3/5, 1/3 pattern and are fine.

it-4ba8.comment: Well judged: the descent crosses 4 onto the long F#4, which already places the thumb for B3, and the chords use standard 1-2-4-5 and 1-2-5 shapes. The black-key thumbs and fifths are forced by the octaves.

objections.problem: Fifth finger on Bb4 in a plain quarter-note line; 2-4 on G4-Bb4 keeps the fifth off the black key.
Thumb plays Bb3 then A3 consecutively, breaking the lower-voice legato and putting the thumb on a black key; 2 on Bb3 avoids both.
Shifting 2-3-4 across the repeated A5s walks the hand for nothing; the F5-C6 five-finger position, 5-4-3-3-3-2-1, needs no shift.
Repeated F5 quarters fingered 2-1-2 swap fingers back and forth for no gain at this tempo; keep the thumb.

it-7c98.comment: Bar 11 needs only small edits, but bars 12-14 juggle fingers on repeated quarter notes, and the A5 and F5 repeats are treated differently. The whole melody from C6 down fits one five-finger position.

it-36c5.comment: Both hands sit in five-finger positions (RH D5-A5 after the octave leap, LH A3-E4) with moves only at the rest and the long notes. Nothing to change.

objections.problem: Fifth finger plays D5 then C5 in consecutive sixteenths; the neighbour-note turn C5-D5-C5-Bb4 is 4-5-4-3.
Thumb passes under 2 onto Bb4 between two A4s and 2 crosses straight back; 2-3-2-1 keeps the turn in one position.
G4 on 2 between two F4s on 3 makes fingers 2 and 3 cross twice in sixteenths; 3-4-3-2 is natural.

it-eca0.comment: Bar 29 is fine, but each of the three turn figures in bar 30 is mis-fingered in a different way. With 4-5-4-3, 2-3-2-1, 3-4-3-2 the sequence gets one consistent shape.

objections.problem: The sequence is fingered 2-4-3-5 three times, then 2-3-2-4 here, so finger 2 creeps from F#4 to G4.

it-1ca6.comment: Clean, position-based fingering with standard 2-over-thumb turns at D5-C5, B4-A4 and G4-F#4. The last group breaks the sequence pattern, which is fine only if bar 5 needs B4 on 4.

objections.problem: Octave G#4-G#5 is given to fingers 2 and 3; 2-3 cannot span more than a fourth.
Thumb is assigned to both Eb4 and Bb4 of one dyad; one finger cannot play two keys a fifth apart.
Eb5 is held by 4 through the beat while 3 plays Bb4, a fourth between 3 and 4. Take Eb5 with 5.
With 5 holding F5, finger 4 on C#5 sits at the 4-5 limit; 3 is more relaxed and matches beat 1.

it-1e1c.comment: Keep the thumb on the repeated G#4 throughout bar 5 and give each bar-6 beat the same 1-3-5 shape under the held melody note. The repeated 5 on the top notes G#5-F5-Eb5 is acceptable here because the afterbeat dyads are detached and pedalled.

objections.problem: The thumb must play D5 while still holding the dotted-half Bb4, and then hops from D5 to Eb5.

it-d598.comment: Bar 2 is well fingered, including 3-4-5 over the held D4-F4. In bar 3, either mark an early release of the lower Bb4 or take D5+F5 with 2+3, sliding 2 off Eb5; 3 on F5 sits a comfortable fourth below the held Bb5.

objections.problem: The A2 octave takes 4+1 here but 5+1 at L19 and L23; in this all-white bar keep 5 throughout.

it-15a2.comment: The RH sequence fingering is textbook, with the one shift at the bar line where the figure moves up. The LH sensibly uses 4 on the F# octaves in bar 20.

objections.problem: Rising E5-F5-G5 is fingered 5-4-3, so 4 crosses over 5 and then 3 over 4, in sixteenths.
E5 on 3 rising to F5 on 2 forces 2 over 3, a long-over-long crossing.

it-146f.comment: The LH and RH bar 15 are sound and stay in one position. RH bar 16 should keep the position the G5 on 4 already sets up: E2 F3 G4 A5 F3 G4 E2 F3.

it-a592.comment: Standard octave fingering: 4 on Bb and Eb gives a legato link down to 5 on G# and C#, and every sequential repeat is fingered the same way.

objections.problem: The sixth E4-C#5 is given to fingers 3 and 2; 2-3 cannot span more than a fourth.
Finger 4 is assigned to both A3 and D4 of the same dyad.
Descending from C#3 on 3 to A2 on 2 crosses 2 over 3, then 5 must jump back above it to E3.

it-14c1.comment: The bar 9 accompaniment is fine. With the fixes, the thumb keeps D4 from E3+D4 into bar 8, 2 fits C#4 between the held A3 and D4, and A2 on 5 leads to the E3 bass with an ordinary bass leap.

it-4129.comment: The thumb anchors A3 and then E3 while 5 takes the bass notes; this is economical and comfortable, and the repeated C3+A3 dyads keep one shape.

objections.problem: Thumb plays E4 then D4 in the falling upper line; with 5 holding G3, 1-2-3-4 keeps the line legato.
Same thumb hop E4 to D4 in the repeated figure; use 1-2-3-4 over the G3 pedal as in bar 13.

it-d39a.comment: Sound hand position over the G3 pedal and identical in both bars; only the repeated thumb on the descending upper voice needs changing.

objections.problem: 1-2 must span the minor sixth A4-F5, then the thumb jumps to D5; an A4-A5 octave position covers the whole figure.
Here 5 takes G3 (F3 in bar 20) although 4 does elsewhere, so 5 shuffles across three keys; 4 keeps the octave position.

it-58b4.comment: The LH pedal figures are well set and treated identically in both bars; the RH broken D-minor chord should stay in one octave position instead of shifting the thumb.

objections.problem: Finger 5 is assigned to both C#3 and G#3 of the held fifth; one finger cannot hold two keys a fifth apart.
With 2 holding A3, B3 on 3 makes a long finger cross over 2; the held fingers end up out of pitch order.
Finger 2 plays A3 then B3 back to back while the thumb is free; the identical figure in bar 21 uses 2-1.

it-7550.comment: The opening chord is impossible and bar 22 crosses 3 over a held 2; once fixed, bars 21 and 23 should share 5+3, 2, 1.

objections.problem: Finger 5 plays D5 then C5 in the falling top line; 4 on C5 keeps the melody legato above the thumb.
Thumb passes under 3 to take A3 although 4 already lies over it in the F3-C4 position; 3-4 is simpler.

it-6878.comment: Chord fingerings in both hands are clear and repeated consistently; only the D5-C5 connection at the end deserves an edit.

it-828c.comment: Careful fingering that respects the held voices and fingers both sequential figures identically; the thumbs on black keys are forced by the chromatic lines.

objections.problem: 4-5 spans the perfect fourth F3-Bb3, beyond a third; 5-3-1 then 4-2 keeps each resolving voice legato.

it-e293.comment: The RH is idiomatic, including the 4-over-thumb crossing into the closing chord; the opening LH chord exceeds the 4-5 span and should be 5-3-1.

objections.problem: Finger 3 on both F#3 and G#3 in one chord; the same dyad on beat 2 already uses 3+2.
4-3 spans the perfect fourth G#3-C#4, beyond a third; 4-2-1 fits this second-inversion shape.

it-a505.comment: Two chords are impossible as written; the remaining bass-and-chord shapes are fine for a waltz.

objections.problem: The repeated G#4 is retaken by the thumb on a black key; keeping 2 and taking D5 with 3 avoids it.
Thirds on 2+5 and 1+2 cramp the hand; 3+5 and 1+3 are standard and match the thirds on beats 3-4.
Finger 3 on both C5 and E5 of the third; continue the 1-3, 2-4 sequence with 3-5.
Finger 2 plays E3 then C3 in the falling A-minor arpeggio; standard 1-2-4-5 keeps it connected.

it-06b9.comment: The LH repeated chords are well fingered, but the closing RH third is impossible and the RH thirds and LH arpeggio need standard patterns.

it-efd1.comment: Each ornament stays in one hand position and the two F#-E turns are fingered alike. 4-3-4 on the turns is fine, though 3-2-3 would be a slightly stronger alternative.

objections.problem: Rising G4 to Bb4 with 3 then 2 makes the index cross over the middle finger, or forces a jump.
Thumb on Bb3 where 2 fits; 2 on Bb3 also frees the thumb to take A3 next without a hop.
Fingers 2 and 3 cannot hold the minor sixth A3-F4 together.
Finger 3 plays G5 and then F5 straight after the sixteenth, breaking the descending line.
Repeated F5 quarters at this tempo need no 3-1-2 changes; jumping to the thumb mid-bar is restless.

it-68c4.comment: The 2+3 sixth in bar 12 is impossible and must be replaced; the opening crossing and the 3-3 hop into F5 also need fixing before this goes to a student.

objections.problem: Both fingers hop from A3+C4 to G3+B3 with 2+1 twice; 3+2 on the second third keeps the pair legato.
3+1 on the minor sixth B3-G4 is a stretch for a medium hand; after the rest 4+1 sits easier.

it-8dfd.comment: Sound overall; give the descending thirds in bar 7 a legato fingering and consider a less stretched choice for the sixth in bar 6.

it-2b0f.comment: Standard 1-3-5 on the E-G#-B shape and a textbook double-third fingering with the thumb passing under at B-C; the jump after the descending run is unavoidable.

it-78dd.comment: The right thumb on the repeated C4 is the sensible choice with the left thumb on Eb4 just above it; the hands interlock, but the fingering itself is sound and the black-key thumbs and fifths in the left hand are unavoidable.

objections.problem: Going from Eb4 down to B3 with 3 then 2 crosses the index over the middle finger at sixteenth speed.
Thumb on C#4 where 2 fits; 3-2-4 on B3-C#4-A3 also matches the 3-2-4 of the next sequence step.
Finger 4 plays G#3 and then C#4 with no break; 2 on C#4 leads smoothly to the thumb on D4.

it-a6ae.comment: The 2-over-3 crossing in bar 3 must go; with 5 on B3 there and 2 on both C#4s in bar 4, the sequence fingers identically and the hop disappears.

it-6cdf.comment: Clear bass-and-chord fingering; the thumb's step from B3 to A3 is the cheapest way into the repeated E3 chords and the closing octave.

objections.problem: 3 on G#3 and 2 on D4 span a diminished fifth, wider than 2-3 allow; the repeat of this chord already uses 4.
4 on F#3 against the thumb on E4 stretches 1-4 across a minor seventh; 5 on F#3 costs only a small bass hop.

it-4617.comment: The right hand uses standard octave and chord fingerings. The left hand has one impossible 2-3 span in the four-note E chord and a stretched 1-4 seventh; both are one-finger fixes.

objections.problem: B4 taken by 4 below finger 3, which still holds Eb5: a long finger crossing under another long finger.
C5 is struck with 3 while 3 is still holding the dotted-eighth Eb5.
C5 held on 3 under F5 on 4: a fourth between fingers 3 and 4 is beyond reach.
F4 and G#4 struck together, both on finger 2; the matching third in bar 8 (R14-15) uses 2+4.

it-77b6.comment: Bar 8 beats 1-2 collide with the held Eb5; 2 on D5 and 1-2 on the inner B4-C5 keep the hand in one place and match the later B4 1 / C5 2. The rest of the sequence is sound once bar 9 ends with 2+4 like bar 8.

objections.problem: G#4 and D5 struck together on finger 5; the identical dyads either side use 5+1.
Octave D4-D5 on fingers 3 and 2; fingers 2-3 reach only about a fourth.

it-f2b2.comment: Bar 1, the held fifth with the inner line on 4-3-2, is well fingered. The two dyad errors in bars 2-3 are the only problems.

objections.problem: 2 crosses over the thumb onto G#4, then the thumb retakes G#4 for the half note; 3-2-2 keeps the thumb off it.
Rising thirds fingered 1/2, 1/3, 2/4 make the thumb hop A4 to B4; standard 1/3, 2/4, 3/5 keeps both voices legato.
Descending arpeggio A3-E3-C3-A2 on 4-1-2-4 passes the thumb under a fourth, then 2 over; 1-2-4-5 needs no crossing.

it-c9e1.comment: The LH repeated chords are fine. The descending arpeggio and the RH thirds want their standard fingerings, and the held G#4 should not sit on the thumb.

objections.problem: D3 on 5 forces a mid-run shift at L10; with D3 on 4 the C3-G3 position covers L6-L21 unchanged.

it-7496.comment: Clean, position-based fingering. Only the entry into the sixteenth figure in bar 20 should be set one step lower to avoid the shift inside the run.

objections.problem: Thumb on D5, then 3 crossing over to C#5 and 4 back on D5 makes the ornament clumsy; 4-3-4-3 stays in one position.

it-312f.comment: Bars 13-14 are well planned, including the 2-1-2-1 turn and the matching 5-4-3 figures in bar 14. Only the opening ornament needs changing.

objections.problem: Bb4 on 3 then D5 on 2: finger 2 must cross over 3 to a higher note at thirty-second speed.
In the turn the thumb passes under 2 onto Eb5; keeping Eb5 on 3, as at R9, stays in one position.

it-c303.comment: The LH is standard mazurka fingering. In the RH, fix the opening Bb-D crossing and keep Eb5 on 3 throughout the turn.

it-0562.comment: One position (D5 on 2 to G5 on 5) carries all of bar 5's ornaments and the line into bar 6, and the two F#-E-F# ornaments are fingered alike. A student may need slow practice to make the 4-3 ornaments even.

objections.problem: E4 and C5 struck together, both on the thumb, a sixth apart.
Octave E4-E5 on 2 and 4, with a tritone on 3-4, is out of reach; the identical chord at R33-35 uses 1+2+5.

it-86b2.comment: Apart from two broken chords in bar 16 the shapes are sensible; the thumb taking the bottom of each chord is normal in slow, pedalled chordal writing. With R21 on 4, bar 16 opens with the same 1+4 / 2+5 pairing as bar 15.

objections.problem: 4-3 spans a fourth (Eb3-G#3) and 4-2 a full octave; a medium hand cannot hold this chord.
Finger 5 is assigned to both Eb3 and G#3 in the same chord.

it-09f3.comment: The repeated LH chord should simply keep 5+3+1 throughout; two chords break this, one with an impossible stretch and one with a doubled finger. The RH thumb on the repeated C4 is the right choice where the hands overlap.

objections.problem: Octave C#4-C#5 on 1-4 with 2 on G4 is a full stretch for a medium hand; 1-2-3-5 is the usual shape.
Octave F#3-F#4 on 1-4 with 1-2 spanning a fifth; 1-3-5 is the natural shape for octave plus fifth.

it-7430.comment: The descending arpeggio and the 3 crossing over the thumb onto F#4 are good, as are the chords around the held F#4. Only the two 1-4 octave chords are too stretched for this student.

it-5541.comment: The RH double notes are fingered naturally, with 5 to 4 legato in the falling sixths. The LH stays in one F position, so Bb3 and A3 fall under 2 and 3 without a shift.

objections.problem: Thumb hops A4 to B4 inside a rising chain of thirds; the standard 1+3, 2+4, 3+5 keeps both voices legato.

it-d587.comment: The descending run and the 2+3 crossing over the thumb onto G#4+B4 are fine. The thirds in bar 15 should use the textbook fingering.

objections.problem: Finger 2 moves F3 to E3 between consecutive chords; 3 already sits over E3 after D3 on 4, so 3+1 needs no move.

it-4c52.comment: Natural bass-and-chord fingering ending on a clean 5+1 octave. Bar 23 refingers the bar-22 opening as 4 / 2+1 because different chords follow, which is reasonable.

objections.problem: Thumb leaves held D5 straight for B4 in the same voice, breaking the legato; 2 on D5 hands over to the thumb.
Thumb leaves held G4 straight for E4 in the lower voice; 2 on G4, with 3 on G#4, keeps it legato.

it-8928.comment: Careful two-voice fingering, and the bar-9 sequence repeats the bar-8 fingering exactly. Only the two thumb leaps in the lower voice break the legato.

objections.problem: The same Bb3+D4 third is 3+1 here but 4+2 at its two repeats; 4+2 from the start keeps 4 on Bb3 throughout.

it-d0f8.comment: Economical: 4 stays on Bb3 and the thumb is free for F4. The 4-2-1 Eb triad keeps the fifth off the black key and is acceptable here.

objections.problem: Fifth finger on black G#4 for the repeated tritone; 4+1 suits the tritone and leads 4 to 3 into A4.

it-cc4b.comment: Bar 1 sits in a clean A five-finger position under the held fifth, and the shift up comes at the rest. The 5 on G#4 works, though 4 is kinder for a beginner.

objections.problem: G4 is a half note on 5, yet 3 plays G#4 above it and 5 is reused on C5 while G4 sounds.
Finger 2 slides F4 to G4 while F4 still sounds; thumb then leaves held D4 for A4 and slides to Bb4.
Thumb moves D5 straight to black-key Eb5 between chords, breaking the legato; 2+4 then 5 connects.

it-ba6c.comment: As notated, the held lower notes in bar 2 cannot be sustained with this fingering; taking the chords 1+2 and the rising line 3-4-5 fixes both spots. Bar 3 works once the thumb hop is smoothed.

objections.problem: E5 is held for a dotted quarter by 3 while 2 plays G#4 and A4 below and 3 is reused on B4.

it-ab75.comment: Sound fugue fingering except the opening: E5 is held over a moving inner voice, so it needs 5 (with 4 on D#5) to free 1-2-3 below it.

it-c25c.comment: Clean, economical fingering; the thumb shift to E4 and the 3-over-1 crossing onto F4 are well placed.

objections.problem: Thumb slides from the held E4 to F4 with no rest, breaking the legato resolution into bar 23.
Six-four chord F3-Bb3-D4 taken 4-2-1; the standard 5-2-1 avoids a sixth between 1 and 4.

it-a13d.comment: Playable and mostly natural; avoid the thumb hop into bar 23 and use the standard 5-2-1 for the six-four chords.

objections.problem: Finger 5 is assigned to both notes of the C2-C3 octave.
Octave Bb1-Bb2 on fingers 3 and 2; 2-3 cannot span an octave. Bar 13 uses 4+1 here.

it-724b.comment: Standard 5-1 / 4-1 octave fingering apart from two impossible octaves; bar 15 should simply repeat bar 13.

it-2d68.comment: Comfortable and consistent; the repeated C3+A3 sixths on 5+1 and the E2-E3 octave are standard.

objections.problem: Minor sixth B3-G4 on fingers 3 and 2; 2-3 cannot span more than a fourth.
Finger 4 is assigned to both G3 and B3 of the same chord.
Finger 5 leaves G3 for C4 with no rest; 4 on C4 keeps the bass line connected.

it-2fa5.comment: The bar 4 broken-chord figure is fine; the chords in bars 6-7 contain two impossible assignments.

objections.problem: Thumb on E5 then 4 on F5 a semitone above cramps the hand; the turn ending sits naturally on 2-3.

it-23db.comment: Consistent arpeggio fingering in bars 5-6; only the turn ending in bar 7 needs a more natural 2-3.

objections.problem: Finger 2 still holds the A4 when asked to play D5, and it would have to cross over 3 on Bb4.
Thumb plays D4, E4 and F4 in succession, two hops in a row; take E4 with 2 and pass the thumb under.

it-c1c5.comment: Bars 5-7 are well fingered and the sequential figures are treated alike. The problems are the thumb slides at the end of bar 8 and the D5 on 2 in bar 9, which collides with the held A4.

objections.problem: 4-3-2 on Bb5-G#5-Eb5 opens a full fourth between 3 and 2 at eighth speed; 5-4-2-1 sits naturally.
The repeated chord C4+Eb4+G#4 switches from 3+2+1 to 4+2+1 for no reason; 3+2+1 suits the position over G#3.

it-08ef.comment: Sound overall, and changing fingers on the repeated Eb5 is right. Prefer the standard 5-4-2-1 shape for the opening descent and finger the two bar-24 chords alike.

it-f57f.comment: Fine as written: the thumb repeats the C4 pedal and the LH keeps one stable 5-3-1 octave shape. The thumbs interlock around C4-Eb4, but that comes from the music, not the fingering.

objections.problem: Finger 4 is assigned to both Bb3 and D4 of the same dyad.
Same Bb3+D4 dyad as L1-2 is fingered 4+2 here; 3+1 every time keeps one hand shape.
4+3+2 on D3+F3+Bb3 stretches both 4-3 and 3-2 to their limits; standard 5-3-1 keeps the thumb on the common Bb3.

it-4694.comment: The 4+4 dyad is impossible, the repeated Bb3+D4 should keep one fingering, and the closing first-inversion chord wants 5-3-1 with the thumb staying on Bb3.

it-258f.comment: Clean waltz fingering: 5 on each bass note, a consistent 3-2-1 or 4-2-1 chord shape chosen by the bottom interval, thumb on top. The black-key thumbs and fifths cannot be avoided here.

objections.problem: Thumb slides E4, D4, C4 in succession over the repeated G3, breaking the upper line; keep 5 on G3 and walk down 1-2-3-4.
Same thumb slides E4, D4, C4 in bar 15; use the one-position fingering proposed for bar 13.
Bar 15 ends G3+B3 on 2+1, while the identical bar 13 uses 4+2; finger both bars alike.

it-66b4.comment: Over the G3 pedal, keep 5 on G3 and let 1-2-3-4 walk down the upper line in a single position; that removes every thumb slide and makes bars 13 and 15 identical.

objections.problem: After 4 on D4, finger 3 stretches a fourth to G4, then 2 must cross 3 to reach F4; the thumb belongs on G4.
Finger 3 plays E4 then G4 on consecutive eighths; the Alberti pattern returns the thumb to G4 as in bar 1.

it-9014.comment: Bar 1 is textbook Alberti 5-1-3-1; bar 2 breaks the pattern twice. With the thumb on every G4 the hand never leaves the C five-finger position.

it-71ef.comment: Standard 5-1 octaves throughout and a sensible 5-4-2-1 for the four-note chord, with the thumb kept on B2 for the last two dyads. Nothing to change for a student who can manage the octave leaps.

it-67bc.comment: Standard sequential fingering: every descending run ends with 2 crossing over the thumb at the same point, so each unit of the sequence sits in a fresh five-finger position.

it-6b3b.comment: Sound double-note fingering: the thumb re-strikes the lower voice, the top line alternates 4 and 5, and 2 stays on the common Bb4 through the octave chords. The black-key thumbs are forced by the harmony.

objections.problem: C-G-E-G Alberti on 4-1-2-1 stretches 4-1 across a fifth; the standard 5-1-3-1 sits in the natural C4-G4 position.
Finger 2 takes D4 and then F4 around the thumb; in the C4-G4 position D4 belongs to 4.

it-24a5.comment: Playable, but the whole figure fits one five-finger position (C=5, D=4, E=3, F=2, G=1), which is what a student should learn here.

it-db9c.comment: Clean: 4-3-2-1 down the broken chord, the usual 3-2-1 finger change on the repeated Eb5, and compact 4-2-1 waltz chords after the 5 in the bass.

objections.problem: Thumb on F#5 a semitone under 4 cramps the hand and adds a 2-over-1 crossing; 4-3-2-1-3 is the standard B-minor arpeggio descent.
D4-F#4-B4-D5 on 2-3-4-5 puts a fourth between 3 and 4 inside a 2-5 octave; too wide for a medium hand.
C#4 and G#4 are both given finger 2 in the same chord.
Octaves C#4-C#5 and F#3-F#4 held 1-4 with inner notes; a strain for a medium hand, 5 on top is safer.

it-9c7d.comment: The last chord assigns finger 2 twice and the D4-D5 chord on 2-3-4-5 cannot be held; the chords want 1 on the bottom and 5 on the top octave throughout.

objections.problem: The thumb holds E4 (whole note) when it must play D4 on beat 3; with 5 on A3 the hand keeps both.

it-f624.comment: Taking the open fifth 5-1 instead of 3-1 gives a held position (5-4-2-1, then 5-3-1 on A-C#-E); the repeated dyads and the octave after the rest are fine.

objections.problem: While 3 holds G4, finger 2 must strike C4 a fifth below; 2-3 cannot span a fifth.
R17-R24 repeat R1-R8 a step higher, but 3-4-5 replaces 2-3-4, so 3 slides from Bb4 straight to A4.

it-f7d3.comment: The two-voice handling in the first bar is good; carry it into the sequence and put 5 on the G4 that is held over the descending bass line.

objections.problem: C5 on 3 right after Bb4 on 4 forces 3 over 4 while 1-2 hold the dyad; 5 is free.
Rising G4-G#4-A4 on 5-4-3 while 2 holds F4: two long-over-long crossings in sixteenths. 3-4-5 fits the position.
Thumb still holds Bb4 (dotted half to beat 4) when it must strike D5 at beat 3.5.

it-a20b.comment: Three spots need rework; with them fixed the passage lies well, with the octave held by 1-5 and the inner descent on 4-3-2.

objections.problem: Finger 5 is assigned to both F#2 and F#3 of a simultaneous octave.
Fingers 3 and 2 cannot hold the octave E2-E3; a 2-3 span reaches only a fourth.

it-78a7.comment: The other octaves and the four-note chord in bar 10 are fingered soundly; the octaves at L3-4 and L7-8 must be 5+1 like the rest.

it-36b7.comment: Sound and idiomatic: the thumb anchors C#5 under the repeated G-Bb dyads and holds it through the 4-5-4 neighbour figure in bar 13.

it-42ad.comment: The leaps in bars 5-6 are fingered consistently (1-4 twice), the turn in bar 8 sits in a natural D-to-G position, and F-A on 1+2 sets up Bb on 3 and D on 5.

objections.problem: Thumb passes under 3 onto F#4, breaking the 1-3-2-4 cell used for the identical figure at R1-R4.
Fingers 3 and 2 cannot hold the octave A2-A3; a 2-3 span reaches only a fourth.
Finger 5 is assigned to both A2 and A3 of a simultaneous octave.

it-3e24.comment: The right-hand sequence is otherwise consistent across both bars; the left-hand octaves should stay 5+1 on white keys and 4+1 on F# throughout.

objections.problem: Finger 2 is assigned to both Bb4 and C5; the same dyad is fingered 2+3 earlier in bar 3.
Fingers 2 and 3 cannot span the sixth F4-D5; a 2-3 span reaches only a fourth.

it-ce72.comment: The left hand is fine. With the two right-hand fixes the sixths move 1+5, 1+5, 1+4 and F4 keeps the thumb.

objections.problem: On E5-A5-E6, 3-4 cannot span a fifth and 2-4 cannot hold an octave; use the 1-2-5 shape used for B-E-B.
Finger 5 is assigned to both E3 and G#3 in the same chord.

it-bff4.comment: Octave and chord fingerings are otherwise standard, with 4 on the black-key octaves for connection; two chords need correcting.

objections.problem: Finger 4 plays G5 then F5 in succession, breaking the legato descent; 4-3-2-1 down to D5 is natural.
Finger 2 is assigned to both E4 and G4 of the dyad.
Fingers 3 and 2 cannot hold the octave Bb2-Bb3; a 2-3 span reaches only a fourth.

it-0ab2.comment: The 5-4-2-1 arpeggio in bar 18 and the left-hand chord shapes are good; three spots need correction before this goes to a student.

objections.problem: Fingers 3 and 2 cannot span the sixth G3-E4; the identical dyad in bar 15 is correctly 5+1.
Finger 5 is assigned to both G3 and D4; the identical dyad in bar 13 is 5+1.

it-c984.comment: Bars 13 and 15 repeat exactly and should share 5+1, 5+1, 5+2, 5+3 over the repeated G3.

it-1ff1.comment: Standard Alberti-bass fingering in a fixed C five-finger position; 4-1-2-1 on D-G-F-G keeps the hand still and the repeated G on the thumb.

objections.problem: Eb5 held by 4 while 3 plays Bb4 below: a perfect fourth between 3 and 4, beyond their third limit.

it-c8b0.comment: Sound for this texture otherwise; the thumb on G#4 and the ninth at R5-6 are forced by the writing. Under the held Eb5 use 1-2-4 (or 5 on Eb5 if a 1-4 octave is too wide).

objections.problem: Bar 21 sequences bar 20 a third higher but drops its 1-3-2-4 shape; the thumb shuttles G4-A4, forcing three needless shifts.

it-b5ca.comment: Bar 20 and the LH octaves are fine. Bar 21 should copy bar 20's 1-3-2-4 shape from G4, with the thumb tucking under 4 at the barline.

objections.problem: Octave B1-B2 fingered 5-4; the 4-5 pair cannot span more than a third.
Octave C2-C3 taken 5-2 is a needless full stretch; plain 5-1 is the standard octave fingering.
Octave A1-A2 fingered 5-3 is beyond a medium hand; it also differs from the repeated A octave at L13-14.

it-05f7.comment: Every octave should be 5-1, as at L1-4 and L13-14. The closing chords L15-22 are well fingered.

objections.problem: Rising A4-C5-F5 fingered 4-3-2 crosses 3 over 4 and 2 over 3; long fingers must not cross.
Grace notes G5 then F5 both on 5: a same-finger hop inside a quick turn.
Thumb jumps up to E5 after the turn and 4 squeezes onto adjacent F5; 2-3 finishes the turn in place.

it-14ad.comment: Bar 6 (2-1-2-3-5) is the model and bar 5 should match it. The bar 7 ornament wants 3-5-3-2-3 under the G5.

objections.problem: C#5 on 3 then D5 on 2 upward makes 2 cross over 3; keep 2 on C#5 as in R2 and R4.
F3 then G3 both on 5 in sixteenths; bar 20's identical figure uses 5-4 here.

it-65d1.comment: Otherwise sound: the LH thumb pedal on E4/D4 with 5-4-3 below is the right shape, and bar 20 is the model for bar 19.

it-b9c8.comment: Sensible: 1-2-4 chords leave 5 free for C6, and the held thumb on C#5 under 4-5-4 is comfortable. Thumb on black keys is forced by the chord shapes.

objections.problem: A3 on 3 leaves 3 and 5 on adjacent keys G3-A3; in this G five-finger position A3 naturally takes 4.

it-3883.comment: Clean and economical; the shifts fall at the rests and the parallel thirds in bar 7 use the standard 3-1 to 4-2.

objections.problem: Opening turn G3-F3-G3 (and F3-E3-F3) on weak 4-5-4, then G3 is re-fingered 3; 3-4-3 keeps one octave position all bar.

it-e1dc.comment: Sound and consistent across the two sequential bars; the right-hand leaps sit well. Only the opening turn of each left-hand bar could use stronger fingers inside a single octave position.

objections.problem: 4-1 on B3-E4 forces the hand up a step at C#4; 5-2 sets the B3-F#4 five-finger position held through L7.

it-3466.comment: Solid fugue fingering; the later thumb moves fall on the quarter and dotted-eighth notes. Starting with 5-2 removes the only unforced shift.

objections.problem: Repeated A5 and F5 fingered 3-3-4 and 2-1-2: needless finger changes and a shift; the F5-C6 five-finger position covers everything.

it-2895.comment: The cadence chords and the leap to C6 after the rest are well handled. The repeated-note fingerings in bars 13-14 are fussy and should be simplified to one position.

it-9d32.comment: Clean: the opening arpeggio keeps the thumb off Bb, the turn sits on 3-4, and the left-hand chords use one shape throughout. The thumb move E4 to F4 comes after a half note, which is the right place for it.

it-fd7a.comment: Standard 5-1 octaves throughout; nothing to change.

objections.problem: 4 on E5 crosses over 3, then 2 crosses back over 4 to G5: illegal long-finger crossings. The sequence elsewhere uses 2-4-3-5.
Finger 3 on G4 then B4 in sixteenths is a hop and breaks the 2-4-3-5 pattern of the other statements.

it-381a.comment: The sequence is well fingered in two of its four statements and the 2-over-thumb descents are fine. Bar 3 beat 2 and the last note need correcting before print.

objections.problem: Thumb must strike C#4 at beat 2 while still holding the dotted-quarter D4; 3 on A3 frees 2 for a legato 4-3 resolution.

it-207b.comment: The descending arpeggio and the bar 9 dyads over the held E3 are well fingered. The only real problem is the suspension in bar 8, which as written asks the thumb to do two things at once.

objections.problem: 2+5 on the third C5-E5 cramps the hand and differs from the 1+3 and 3+5 thirds used at R12-R17.
Re-striking G#4 with the thumb puts it on a black key for a half note; keeping 2 is simpler for a student.

it-429f.comment: Left hand is standard throughout. In the right hand the thirds of bar 5 should share one fingering, and the thumb on G#4 is unnecessary.

objections.problem: Thumb still holds the half-note C#5 when it is asked to strike Bb5; one finger cannot hold both.
2-3 across the tritone C#5-G5 strains on a held chord; 1+3+5 matches the C#5=1, G5+Bb5=3+5 pattern that follows.

it-57e1.comment: The waltz figure lies well once the bar-12 chord matches the following C#5=1, G5+Bb5=3+5 pattern. The thumb on Bb5 in bar 13 is impossible while it holds C#5; 4 there gives Bb5-C6-Bb5 as 4-5-4.

objections.problem: Finger 3 still holds the dotted-eighth D5 when it must strike Eb5; D5 on 2 lets both voices sound full value.
Finger 2 moves straight from D5 to C5 at the dyad; 4-3 on Eb5-D5 then 2+4 keeps both voices legato.
Same 2-2 hop from G4 to F4 in the sequence a fifth lower; fix it the same way.

it-53b9.comment: A well-planned two-voice fingering with consistent sequence fingering and the thumb always on white keys. Fix the opening D5 so it can be held under Eb5, and remove the 2-2 hop into each beat-4 dyad.

it-bb8c.comment: Sound and simple: 3+1 on the repeated staccato dyads with the thumb moving only during rests, and 5+3+2 keeps the thumb off Bb3 in both chords.

objections.problem: Alternating 2-1 makes the hand shift on nearly every sixteenth; bar 3 sits in one B3-F#4 five-finger position.
The same 2-1 seesaw in bar 4; 4 on A3 and G#3, 3 on B3, 2 on C#4, 1 on D4 needs no shift.
Thumb lands on black Eb4 and C#4 in fast sixteenths where 3 and 2 fall on them naturally.

it-3a6d.comment: Fingered almost entirely 2-1, so the hand seesaws on every sixteenth at a fast tempo. Both bars sit in compact positions that need no shifts at all.

objections.problem: LH 4-5-4-3 on A3-F4-E4-D4 runs the fingers backwards: 5 crosses over 4, then 4 and 3 cross leftward.
Finger 4 plays E3 then F3 in consecutive sixteenths, a hop; 3 on F3 keeps the line legato.

it-03e4.comment: From the ninth leap onward the fingering is good, and the 5-5 bass leap at the cadence is fine. The opening of bar 20 runs the fingers backwards and the 4-4 hop should go.

objections.problem: Ornament D5-C#5-D5-C#5 taken 1-2-1-3 crosses over the thumb twice at 32nd speed; 4-3-4-3 lies naturally.
4 on F#4 has to cross over 3 on G4 inside the quick turn: a long-finger crossing.
Thumb on C#5 is avoidable; 2 takes it and 2-5 easily spans the tritone to G5.
Finger 2 plays E5 then jumps a fourth to A5 with no break.
3 on F#5 must cross over 2 on A5, a long-finger crossing.

it-352b.comment: Several spots work against the hand: the ornament on the thumb, two long-finger crossings and a hop. Each fix is local, and the rest of the line (C#5-B4-A4 as 3-2-1, E5 on 5) is fine.

objections.problem: E3 and A3 are struck together with finger 3; one finger cannot play two non-adjacent keys.
Octave A2-A3 on 3 and 2 is far beyond any 2-3 span; take it 5+1.

it-2377.comment: The bass-plus-chord pattern (5, then 3+1) and the 4+1, 4+2 dyads are sensible. Two spots are impossible: the 3+3 dyad in bar 22 and the 3+2 octave at the end.

objections.problem: 1-4 octaves on C# are good legato technique but a stretch for a medium hand; a student can play them 1-5.
Re-fingering E3+G#3+D4 from 5+3+1 to 5+4+2+1 one eighth later shifts the hand; take it 5+4+2 from the start.

it-a805.comment: Idiomatic octave-and-chord fingering in both hands; the LH inner D4 on the free 2 under the held chord is well judged. Only small preferences for a student with a medium hand.
